children: State Bank of India Sponsored GDR RegS (NSE:SBIN) faces a complex week as Bernstein links UPI MDR changes to an ~80bn INR issuer pool with SBIN poised to capture ~25%, while SBIN GDRs see trimmed offer sizes in NSE sell-offs amid a stranded $300M Moscow dividend and market moves tied to a fake merger note.
: Bernstein estimates India’s new MDR on UPI could create an ~80bn INR issuer pool; SBI Sponsored GDR RegS (SBIN) may capture ~25% (~20bn INR). Banks may retain ~60% of annual payments profit.
: SBIN GDRs included among 23 sellers in NSE offer-for-sale aiming to raise up to ₹22,562 crore; SBI and SBI Capital Markets listed as selling shareholders.
: SBIN holds a stranded $300M dividend in its Moscow branch linked to Oil India’s stake in two Russian assets; funds can’t be repatriated due to Western sanctions and banking limits.
: SBIN rose ~1% to an intraday high near Rs 993 as PSU bank stocks rallied amid circulation of a fake merger document; move noted as market reaction, not confirmed corporate action.
: SBIN GDR: updated offer docs show reduced seller allocations and a lower total offer; several institutions cut proposed sale amounts, reflected in the revised seller schedule and quantities.
: SBIN acted as subscriber for a $150M Maldives T‑Bill facility (2019). Final $50M repayment settled Sept 17; India paid about $45M in interest over five years.
